I’m a 58-year-old farmer in Quzhou, and I’ve worked this land for 30 years. My family has six people, but my son and daughter-in-law work in a factory in Handan city, so it’s mostly me and my wife in the fields now, though they come back for harvest if they can get leave. We have 12.4 mu and a well that gives us water when the rain doesn’t come.

Cotton is what I know best—Quzhou soil is good for it, and even though prices go up and down, it’s still our main cash crop. I’ll put 7 mu into Bt hybrid cotton this year. I’ll rotary-till the fields and plant in late April. Cotton is hungry for fertilizer, so I’ll put down compound fertilizer and topdress urea at flowering. With the well, I can irrigate four times, which is crucial in July and August when the bolls are setting. I’ll spray pesticides about seven times—even with Bt seed, we still get aphids and spider mites out here.

I keep 3 mu in winter wheat. It’s already in the ground since last October, so right now I need to topdress nitrogen at green-up and irrigate three times before harvest in early June. I use improved varieties that don’t lodge. After we cut the wheat, I won’t waste any time—I’ll plant summer maize the same week, direct-seeding without plowing to catch the moisture. Hybrid maize seed is expensive but worth it. It needs water at tasseling, so I’ll irrigate three times.

I’ll plant 1.8 mu of peanut in the spring on the sandier patch near the well. Peanut brings good money, and the oil is useful at home too. It needs phosphate for the pods and some potash. I’ll irrigate three times.

For mung bean, I’ll sow 0.6 mu along the edges of the cotton field or between rows in early summer. It doesn’t need much—just a little fertilizer and one irrigation if it gets too dry. It gives a small harvest and helps the soil.

My plan keeps labor manageable. Wheat and maize are on the same 3 mu, cotton and peanuts are on their own plots, and mung bean fits in the gaps. With the children away, I can’t do anything too complicated, but this system has fed my family for decades and it will this year too.
